1.say: Lay the two white wires on the work mat. Strip about one centimetre from each white wire end with the stripper.
placements: white insulated wire left piece → stripped about one centimetre at its lower end with blue and red stripper jaws exposing copper; in the video: left side of light blue mat
white insulated wire right piece → stripped about one centimetre at its lower end with blue and red stripper jaws exposing copper; in the video: right side of light blue mat
watch_for: if copper strands are cut or missing, the stripper closed too deep; restrip a fresh end to leave full copper.
if white insulation still covers the tip, you stripped too little; you should see about one centimetre of clean copper.
1.check_yourself: Two white wires lie apart on the mat with about one centimetre of clean copper showing at each joining end.
1.safety: Keep fingers clear of the stripper jaws because the cutting edges are sharp.

2.say: Push the two copper ends of the white wires together end to end. Twist the copper round to lock the white wires into one loop.
placements: stripped copper ends of the two white wires → pushed together end to end then twisted round each other at centre of mat forming one loop; in the video: copper join at bottom centre of the white wire circle
watch_for: if the wires pull apart with a light tug, the copper was not twisted enough; retwist until it holds.
if white insulation overlaps the join, the ends were not met tip to tip; redo so only copper twists.
2.check_yourself: The two white wires form one loop with the copper ends twisted into a small neat join in the middle.

3.say: Hold the white wire loop steady on the mat. Dab flux onto the twisted copper join with the black stick.
placements: solder flux → dabbed to coat the twisted copper join at centre of white wire loop; in the video: bottom centre of loop on light blue mat applied with thin black stick
watch_for: if the join still looks dry and dull, you used too little flux; add another small dab until it looks wet.
if flux spreads onto the white insulation, you used too much; wipe the wire and keep flux only on copper.
3.check_yourself: The twisted copper join looks wet and shiny in the middle of the white wire loop.
3.safety: Keep flux off your skin and out of your eyes.

4.say: Hold the tinned iron tip against the fluxed copper join. Feed the thin silver solder wire to the hot join. Hold heat until the solder spreads along the whole join.
placements: tinned soldering iron tip → held against the twisted copper join at bottom centre of white wire loop; in the video: copper coloured iron approaching from top centre
thin silver solder wire → fed to the heated join until coating spreads along and around copper; in the video: fine wire fed from right side of join on light blue mat
watch_for: if solder balls up and will not spread, the join is too cold or lacks flux; reheat a little longer with flux.
if white insulation near the join melts back, the iron was held too long; heat only the copper.
4.check_yourself: The centre join is covered with shiny silver solder joining the white wires with no copper showing.
4.safety: Never touch the hot iron tip or fresh solder.

5.say: Push the short black tube onto one white wire end. Slide the black tube along to centre it over the silver join. Leave white insulation showing past both ends of the tube.
placements: short black heat shrink tube → slid over one free end of white wire then centred over soldered join leaving white insulation exposed on both sides; in the video: black tube at bottom centre of white wire loop on light blue mat
watch_for: if the black tube will not fit over the join, the tube is too small; use a wider tube that slides freely.
if silver solder shows past the tube, the tube is off centre; slide it until white insulation shows on both sides.
5.check_yourself: A loose black tube covers the soldered join with white insulation visible on both sides.

6.say: Hold the white wire steady beside the black tube. Move the hot gun nozzle gently along the black tube until it shrinks tight.
placements: hot air gun metal nozzle → held just above and moved gently along black tube over join until tight; in the video: silver and black gun approaching from top left above bottom centre of loop
watch_for: if the black tube stays loose, heat was too brief or too far away; reheat slowly until it grips.
if the white insulation melts or browns, heat was too close or too long; lift the nozzle higher and keep moving.
6.check_yourself: The black sleeve is shrunk tight around the white wire with no solder showing and no loose movement.
6.safety: Keep fingers and the nozzle off the hot tube and keep the heat moving.
